page.overview:
Who is Anwat?

Born as a sandbender, Anwat was among the tribespeople whose families had settled down in Liyuan. In his childhood, Anwat's grandmother taught him how to use various plants of the Si Wong Desert to create medicine. Once he was an adult, he joined Liyuan's ad hoc militia under Bai Yin Du who implored all militia members to use traditional earthbending instead of sandbending, believing the former to be superior.

When Kya came to Liyuan in the 130s AG to teach modern medical techniques to the locals, Anwat was among her pupils. During her first lesson, Anwat revealed his knowledge on traditional Si Wong healing and was encouraged by Kya to share his skills with the class. Over the following time, he attentively attended the waterbender's lessons.

One day, however, Kya's lessons were disrupted by an alarm, as raiders had arrived at Liyuan's eastern fields. Like other locals, Anwat rushed to the fields to take up arms against the attackers. He and the rest of the militia battled the attackers. Ultimately, the raiders successfully stole one of Liyuan's crucial water tanks and escaped on their sand-sailers. To pursue them and recapture the water, Bai Yin declared her intention to recruit more benders into the militia from the surrounding pro-Earth Kingdom clans. As one of the few militia members who had not been wounded in the clash, Anwat was selected to accompany this mission.

Anwat, Bai Yin, Tsetseg, and Kya subsequently moved to a traditional Si Wong meeting place with two sand-sailers. They managed to recruit a young sandbender, Dorzhi. The group continued their journey until evening, when they set up camp at a small stone overcrop. They were surprised by a rattle jackal which promptly attacked, biting Dorzhi and injecting its venom. The rest of the group managed to fend off the creature and they fled onto their sand-sailers, returning to the open desert. Kya attempted to heal Dorzhi but discovered that her waterbending was blocked. In response, Anwat suggested muri bean leaves as an alternate treatment, having learned from his grandmother that this plant could serve as an antidote for rattle jackal bites. While Dorzhi suffered growing pain and fever due to the venom, Anwat managed to gather some leaves from the surrounding desert. The group was able to create ad hoc medicine and successfully cared for the young sandbender, though the boy remained deeply weakened.
